stem: The patty pan squash plant, *Cucurbita pepo*, produces edible fruits that vary in colour.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem:
The colour of the fruits is controlled by two genes, $A/a$ and $B/b$, that occur on different chromosomes.

• Allele $A$ produces a white fruit colour.
• Allele $a$ does not produce a colour by itself but allows the colours coded by gene $B/b$ to show in the phenotype.
• Allele $B$ produces a yellow fruit colour.
• Allele $b$ produces a green fruit colour.

In a dihybrid cross, an $AABB$ plant was crossed with an $aabb$ plant. All the resulting F1 plants produced white fruits.

The F1 plants were then crossed with each other to obtain the F2 generation.
parts.text:
Complete Fig. 2.1 with the gametes produced by the F1 parents, the F2 genotypes and the F2 phenotypes.

State the ratio of fruit colours in the F2 offspring.

F1 parents: $AaBb$ × $AaBb$

Fig. 2.1

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
Test crosses were carried out on two white-fruited plants, $P$ and $Q$, from the F2 generation. Each of these plants had its female flowers pollinated with pollen from a green-fruited plant.

For plant $P$, half of the offspring were white and half were yellow.
For plant $Q$, half of the offspring were white and half were green.

Deduce the genotypes of plants $P$ and $Q$.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text:
Plants $P$ and $Q$ show genetic variation with respect to fruit colour alleles.

Identify the process that occurred during meiosis in the F1 parents that produced this variation **and** the stage of meiosis at which it occurred.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
In 1994, two new varieties of squash were grown in the USA. Both varieties showed resistance to two viral diseases of squash plants.

• The variety 'Tigress' was developed by selective breeding.
• The variety 'Freedom II' was developed by adding genes for viral coat proteins to the squash genome.
parts.text: Identify, with reasons, the variety of squash that can be described as recombinant.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Outline **one** social advantage and **one** social disadvantage of the recombinant squash variety compared to non-resistant squash varieties.
